text:
Thomas Harley played 30:54 against Florida on November 15 when Dallas was down to five defensemen, and "That's My Job" was how the Dallas Hoops Journal headlined his reaction. Four nights later he tied the game against Vegas late with a shot from distance, and the Stars won in a shootout. Dallas has won nine of his last ten games, and he's been at the center of it: ten points in that stretch, 26.4 minutes a night.

Overall he has 3 goals and 15 points in 23 games. The numbers say most of it is honest. His shooting (7%) is inside his likely range, the team's on-ice luck is close to neutral, and at 5v5 the Stars take 53% of the expected goals with him on, four and a half points better than without him. His points rate is a touch above what we think he is (1.5 per 60 against about 1.35), so the last ten is likely his peak.

The question from last season was defense: Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more chances with him on the ice (bottom 10% of defensemen). So far this year, that hasn't shown up.
